title: Gaussian Elimination & LU Decomposition
description: Forward/back substitution, LU decomposition, pivoting, Cholesky decomposition, computational cost.
html:
🧮 Gaussian Elimination & LU Decomposition

1. Triangular Systems

Back substitution for $Ux = y$: $x_i = \frac{1}{u_{ii}}\bigl(y_i - \sum_{j>i} u_{ij}x_j\bigr)$. Forward substitution for $Ly = b$. Cost $n^2$.

2. LU Decomposition

$$l_{ik} = \frac{a_{ik}^{(k)}}{a_{kk}^{(k)}}, \quad a_{ij}^{(k+1)} = a_{ij}^{(k)} - l_{ik}a_{kj}^{(k)}, \quad A = LU$$

$L$: unit lower triangular matrix holding the factors (positive), $U$: upper triangular matrix. Cost $\frac23 n^3$.

Example

$$\begin{pmatrix}2&1&1\\4&3&3\\8&7&9\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\2&1&0\\4&3&1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}2&1&1\\0&1&1\\0&0&2\end{pmatrix}$$

Solving: $Ly = b$ (forward), $Ux = y$ (backward), $O(n^2)$ per right-hand side. Never form $A^{-1}$ explicitly.

3. Pivoting

$PA = LU$

Partial pivoting: swap the entry of largest magnitude to the top, then $|l_{ik}| \le 1$. Reorder $b$ with $P$: $Ly = Pb$. Without swaps it exists only if all leading principal minors are $\ne 0$.

4. Cholesky and Special Cases

$$A = LL^T, \quad l_{jj} = \sqrt{a_{jj} - \sum_{k

For symmetric positive definite matrices, $\frac13 n^3$ flops, no pivoting. Tridiagonal systems: $O(n)$. Determinant: $\det A = \pm\prod u_{ii}$.

5. Typical Mistakes

  • Wrong sign of the factors in $L$.
  • Forgetting to apply the permutation to $b$ in $PA = LU$.
  • Using Cholesky for a non-symmetric or non-positive-definite matrix.
  • Computing $A^{-1}$ explicitly instead of solving $Ax = b$.
